questions.question: Glucagon, a peptide hormone, is produced by the ______.
questions.solution: Glucagon is a hormone secreted by the alpha cells of the pancreas. It works to increase blood glucose levels by stimulating the liver to convert glycogen into glucose.

questions.question: Which hormone is secreted by the brain to help regulate sleep-wake cycles?
questions.solution: Melatonin is produced by the pineal gland in the brain. Its production increases in response to darkness, helping to regulate the body's circadian rhythm and sleep patterns.

questions.question:
Match the columns:
Column-A (Enzyme)Column-B (Role)
i. Helicasea. Joins DNA fragments
ii. RNA primaseb. Nucleotide polymerisation
iii. DNA polymerasec. RNA primer synthesis
iv. DNA ligased. Opens DNA double helix
questions.solution:
The correct functions are:
  • Helicase: Unwinds/opens the DNA helix.
  • RNA Primase: Synthesizes RNA primers.
  • DNA Polymerase: Adds nucleotides to the growing DNA strand.
  • DNA Ligase: Joins DNA fragments together.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the BCG vaccine:
1. It is used for protection against Malaria.
2. It was developed by Albert Calmette and Camille Guérin.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution: Statement 1 is incorrect because the BCG vaccine is used for protection against Tuberculosis (TB), not Malaria. It was indeed developed by Calmette and Guérin in 1921.

questions.question: Which of the following is an inactivated (killed) polio vaccine developed in 1952?
questions.solution: The Salk vaccine (Inactivated Polio Vaccine - IPV) was developed by Jonas Salk. The Sabin vaccine is the oral (live-attenuated) version.

questions.question: Who described the algae Spirogyra in 1674 and named the motile organisms 'Animalcules'?
questions.solution: Anton van Leeuwenhoek was the first scientist to observe and describe microorganisms (bacteria and protists) using his handcrafted microscopes, calling them 'animalcules'.

questions.question: Around which year did Robert Brown publish a paper highlighting the presence of a nucleus in plant cells?
questions.solution: Robert Brown described the cell nucleus in detail in 1831 during a talk at the Linnean Society of London.

questions.question: Who explained the structure of protein (alpha helix and beta sheet)?
questions.solution: Linus Pauling and Robert Corey proposed the secondary structures of proteins, the alpha helix and beta sheet, in 1951.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. G.N. Ramachandran was an Indian physicist who worked in structural biology.
2. He discovered the fluid mosaic model of cell membrane.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution: Statement 1 is correct. However, Statement 2 is incorrect because G.N. Ramachandran discovered the triple helical structure of collagen and created the Ramachandran plot. The fluid mosaic model was proposed by Singer and Nicolson.

questions.question: In 1873, who published the first photograph of nerve tissue stained with the black reaction technique?
questions.solution: Camillo Golgi developed the 'black reaction' (silver nitrate stain) which allowed for the first clear visualization of the entire nerve cell structure.

questions.question: Which cytologist demonstrated the role of the Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER) in protein processing in the 1960s?
questions.solution: George E. Palade is known for his pioneering work in cell biology, particularly the function of the Endoplasmic Reticulum and ribosomes, for which he won a Nobel Prize in 1974.

questions.question: In 1906, Camillo Golgi shared the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with whom?
questions.solution: Camillo Golgi and Santiago Ramón y Cajal shared the 1906 Nobel Prize for their independent but complementary work on the structure of the nervous system.

questions.question: In which year did Rudolf Virchow formulate the aphorism 'Omnis cellula-e cellula' (all cells come from cells)?
questions.solution: Rudolf Virchow added the final tenet to the Cell Theory in 1855, stating that new cells are formed only from the division of pre-existing cells.

questions.question: In which year did Gorter and Grendel conclude that the lipid surface surrounding cells must be a bilayer?
questions.solution: In 1925, E. Gorter and F. Grendel performed experiments on red blood cells and proposed that the cell membrane is composed of a lipid bilayer.

questions.question: Who published research in 1956 defining 46 as the exact number of human chromosomes?
questions.solution: Joe Hin Tjio (along with Albert Levan) accurately determined that humans have 46 chromosomes (23 pairs) in 1956, correcting the previous belief that there were 48.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about Helicobacter pylori:
1. It was discovered by Barry Marshall and Robin Warren.
2. It is responsible for causing chronic gastritis and peptic ulcers.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. Marshall and Warren proved that H. pylori bacteria, not just stress or acid, cause most stomach ulcers, for which they won a Nobel Prize.

questions.question: In which year did Walther Flemming coin the term 'chromatin'?
questions.solution: Walther Flemming coined the term chromatin in 1879 to describe the stainable substance in the cell nucleus that forms chromosomes.

questions.question: Which ecologist is famous for studying plant life in the Indiana Dunes in 1896?
questions.solution: Henry Chandler Cowles was a pioneer in ecology who studied ecological succession in the Indiana Dunes.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about Jagadish Chandra Bose (JC Bose):
1. He is regarded as the Father of Indian Plant Physiology.
2. He invented the crescograph to measure plant growth.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.solution: Both statements are correct. JC Bose made significant contributions to plant physiology and invented the crescograph to record minute variations in plant growth.

questions.question: Which among the following are commonly known as blood thinners?
questions.solution: Anticoagulants are medications that prevent or reduce the coagulation of blood, effectively acting as blood thinners to prevent clots.

questions.question: For what discovery was Jan Evangelista Purkinje known in 1839?
questions.solution: In 1839, Jan Evangelista Purkinje coined the term 'protoplasm' for the fluid substance found inside a cell.

questions.question: Who explained the structure and reproductive system of algae in 1935?
questions.solution: F.E. Fritsch published the comprehensive work 'The Structure and Reproduction of the Algae' in 1935, providing a major classification system for algae.

questions.question: Which ecologist’s research provided revolutionary new insights into how energy and nutrients move through the ecosystems?
questions.solution: Raymond Laurel Lindeman is credited with providing seminal insights into trophic dynamics, explaining how energy and nutrients move through various levels of an ecosystem. His work is a cornerstone of modern ecosystem ecology.

questions.question: In 1857, who was the first to experimentally demonstrate that yeast is responsible for alcohol production and that contaminating microorganisms can cause sour fermentation?
questions.solution: Louis Pasteur discovered that microorganisms cause fermentation and diseases. He demonstrated that yeast produces alcohol and developed the process of pasteurisation to kill harmful microbes in food.

questions.question: In 1838, who published an article discussing the structure and origin of plant cells?
questions.solution: Matthias Schleiden (in 1838) and Theodor Schwann (in 1839) co-founded the Cell Theory. Schleiden specifically defined the cell as the basic unit of plant structure.
